statement: The proportion of SUID cases involving infants who slept with an adult was higher compared to the general population of live-born infants in 2015.
rationale: This design compares the prevalence of infant sleep-sharing with adults among SUID cases (from ncfrp_v51) and a general population sample of live-born infants (from prams_p7_arf), using cdc_linkco15 as the denominator source for both groups in 2015.
prior_art: The closest tested work is bedsharing_ms_v7.C8, which notes that bed sharing was recorded for 59.5% of SUID cases but does not provide a direct comparison with the general population. This question remains open as it seeks to quantify this difference relative to live-born infants.
cannot_establish: The design cannot establish causality; it can only compare proportions or odds of exposure among cases versus the general population.
